findings.evidence: The circle proof must write `letI : Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup N ℝ x) := HomotopyGroup.subsingleton_of_topologicalVectorSpace` (HigherHomotopy.lean:56–57) precisely because it is not an instance, then falls back to `inferInstance` on line 59.
findings.fix: Mark it `instance`. The resolution is terminal (no loop) and keyed on the TVS instances.
findings.issue: `subsingleton_of_topologicalVectorSpace` is a `theorem`, not an `instance`. A `Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup N E x)` fact whose hypotheses are all typeclasses (all of E, x, N are determined by the target type) is the canonical instance; as a plain theorem no consumer can obtain the triviality by instance resolution and must `letI` it manually.

findings.evidence: Declared `theorem subsingleton_homotopyGroup : Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup N (AddCircle p) x)`; no `instance` form of the triviality is exposed (grep for `Subsingleton (π_`/`Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup` finds no instance).
findings.fix: Mark `subsingleton_homotopyGroup` (and correspondingly `subsingleton_homotopyGroupPi`) `instance`; `p` and `x` are fixed by the target type and `[Nontrivial N]` is a fine instance premise.
findings.issue: `subsingleton_homotopyGroup` (and thus `subsingleton_homotopyGroupPi`) is a `theorem`, so `Subsingleton (π_ (n+2) (AddCircle p) x)` cannot be found by instance search downstream — same gap as the TVS lemma.

summary: Minimal surface, bodies hidden, characteristic API otherwise complete. But the two `Subsingleton` results are plain theorems, so the triviality facts are unavailable to typeclass resolution — the PR itself has to `letI` one in by hand.
